text:
sara: quick check — i'm sketching the console flow for automatic fallback policies. want to validate UX assumptions before i wire it up. main questions: how much detail do we show by default, and how do we surface auditability without spamming teams? :thinking:

ben: agree we need a compact default view. show current policy + live status. advanced panel for triggers/conditions and historical playbacks. :+1:

amy: i worry about noise. ops should get the high-signal alerts (when fallback rate > 1% for 5m). default should summarize: "status: healthy / degraded / fallback-active" then a single-line reason. links to expandable audit.

jordan: thinking about progressive disclosure — card in service detail: header with state, small pill with reason, chevron to expand timeline + sampled request traces. Add a playback button that replays decisioning in a sandbox.

raul: telemetry note — the console needs a compact fingerprint for each fallback event so audit playback can reconstruct decisions without shipping PII. suggest storing: model_variant, triggered_signal, threshold, request_id_sample, timestamp. that should be enough to replay decisions.

sara: +1. also we need a way for teams to set quiet windows (slo-aware) and an allowlist for noisy routes. UI should expose those as toggles.

ben: API debate: do we return the full policy evaluation for every request in the response trace, or only emit evaluation events to telemetry? Perf-wise i'd rather keep runtime lightweight and emit evaluation events async. then console composes playback from events.

amy: agreed — runtime should be minimal. playback can pull events from the audit store. UX should clearly label that playback is a reconstruction (not necessarily exact live timing).

jordan: mock idea — collapsed row example:
```
[Service] Search API • state: fallback-active • reason: latency spike (p90>700ms)
[▸] Show details
```
On expand: timeline, top 3 triggers, last 5 sampled requests, a "reconstruct decision" button that opens a safe sandbox with read-only request context.

raul: about triggers — we need guardrails for oscillation. UI should surface a probation window and a rollback heater: if fallback toggles >3 times in 15m, system auto-suggests a pause/lock. show that suggestion inline.

ben: small config snippet i proposed for the API (for product to review):
```yaml
policy:
  name: auto-fallback-v1
  modes:
    - gentle-degrade
    - full-fallback
  triggers:
    latency_p90_ms: 700
    error_rate_pct: 2.0
  probation_window_sec: 900
  oscillation_threshold: 3
  audit_sampling_rate: 0.01
```
This keeps runtime fast (low sampling) and lets playback reconstruct from sampled events.

amy: UX question — do we show sampled event links inline (so engs can click to see request content) or put a security barrier to request preview?

raul: must be gated. Default hide sensitive fields and require role-based access to full payload. add a redaction toggle in the audit view.

jordan: also add a small "why this matters" hint next to the sampling rate explaining tradeoffs: more sampling = better repro but higher cost + privacy surface. short tooltip does it.

ben: rollout plan for the console: 1) read-only playback from sampled events, 2) add edit policy in console (disabled by default), 3) canary rollout for 10% of orgs, monitor fallback telemetry.

deploy-bot: canary rollout deployed to staging for auto-fallback-console v0.3 — tests: 128 passed, 2 flaky. link: https://ci.internal/r/2345 :rocket:

sara: thanks — next steps: i'll produce a compact mock (card + expand) and a spec for telemetry fields (raul can review). aim for PR by EOD Friday. tagging @ben @jordan for API/visual review. :eyes:
